skill.name: extension-posting-to-x
skill.description: Build Caffeine canisters that post to X through x-client, per-user OAuth 2.0 PKCE, protected token storage, and non-replicated outcalls.
skill.summary: Guide Caffeine apps through per-user X posting with Motoko, OAuth 2.0 PKCE, and the x-client package.
skill.author: caffeinelabs

security_audit.summary: All 247 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown notation, official reference URLs, normal relative links, or Motoko syntax. No static match represents command execution, unsafe filesystem access, reconnaissance, or unrelated network traffic. Semantic review found overbroad agent-control directives and an OAuth callback design that omits the state value required for CSRF validation.

remediation.issue: Agent-routing text suppresses normal refusal and retrieval decisions.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the directives to never decline, deflect, or call query_rag. Scope activation to explicit X posting requests and preserve higher-priority safety and routing policy.

remediation.issue: The canonical OAuth callback cannot verify the returned state value.
remediation.suggestion: Add state to completeXOAuth and the frontend call. Bind one-time state to the caller, then reject missing, mismatched, reused, or expired values before exchange.

remediation.issue: OAuth authorization, exchange, and refresh functions are deployment-blocking stubs.
remediation.suggestion: Provide reviewed implementations or require a trusted implementation source. Validate redirect URIs, PKCE values, token responses, expiry, and refresh rotation before deployment.

content.user_title: Build Secure X Posting for Caffeine Apps
content.value_statement: Direct X API integration can expose bearer tokens, multiply outcall costs, and mishandle optional fields. This skill provides Motoko architecture, OAuth guidance, frontend flows, and x-client patterns for secure per-user posting.
actual_capabilities: Installs and configures x-client 0.2.3 for X API v2 posting.
Compares admin, per-user, and fallback Client ID architectures.
Defines per-user OAuth 2.0 PKCE token storage and refresh behavior.
Provides Motoko scaffolding for configuration, authentication, posting, and disconnection.
Requires non-replicated HTTP outcalls to protect tokens and control costs.
Maps backend variants to login, settings, connection, and posting interfaces.
limitations: The OAuth authorization, token exchange, and refresh functions are stubs that require implementation.
The skill focuses on X writes and does not cover timelines, search, or general user lookup.
It requires a Caffeine Internet Computer project, Motoko, and the authorization extension.
It does not create an X Developer App or verify a deployed integration.

use_cases.title: Add posting to a community app
use_cases.description: Implement signed-in posting through one operator-managed X Developer App while keeping each member's OAuth tokens isolated.

use_cases.title: Separate tenant rate limits
use_cases.description: Use per-user Client IDs so tenants control their X applications and do not share one rate-limit pool.

use_cases.title: Standardize X integration
use_cases.description: Define approved backend, OAuth, and frontend patterns for teams building X posting into Internet Computer applications.

prompt_templates.title: Plan basic X posting
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan X posting for my Caffeine app. Use the admin Client ID variant and list required backend, authentication, and frontend work.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for one shared X Developer App

prompt_templates.title: Build the default architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the admin Client ID and per-user OAuth architecture. Include token isolation, non-replicated outcalls, connection status, posting, and disconnection.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt for multiple tenants
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the X posting design for per-user Client IDs. Explain storage, caller checks, OAuth routing, rate-limit isolation, and the settings experience.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an existing integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Caffeine X integration for token exposure, OAuth state verification, PKCE handling, redirect validation, refresh rotation, replicated outcalls, authorization, and incomplete stubs.

output_examples.input: Add X posting to a community application with one operator-managed Developer App.
output_examples.output: Use the admin Client ID variant. Each signed-in member completes OAuth separately, while the canister stores tokens by principal and mediates every post.

output_examples.input: Our tenants need independent X API quotas and their own Developer Apps.
output_examples.output: Use per-user Client IDs. Provide personal settings and connection pages, then resolve each caller's Client ID before starting OAuth or posting.

output_examples.input: Check whether our callback flow protects against OAuth login CSRF.
output_examples.output: Verify that the server creates a one-time state value, binds it to the caller, and rejects callbacks with missing, mismatched, or expired state.

best_practices: Use x-client 0.2.3 or later and keep posting outcalls non-replicated.
Store access and refresh tokens only in canister state keyed by the authenticated caller.
Generate and verify one-time OAuth state and PKCE values on the server before token exchange.
anti_patterns: Do not expose, return, log, or persist OAuth bearer tokens in the browser.
Do not use replicated HTTP outcalls for authenticated X requests.
Do not deploy placeholder OAuth functions or accept callback parameters without server-side validation.

faq.question: Does this skill read timelines or search X?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on X write operations. Use a general HTTP outcall integration for unsupported read endpoints.

faq.question: Where are OAuth tokens stored?
faq.answer: Store them in canister state keyed by the authenticated caller. Never return them to the frontend.

faq.question: Which Client ID variant should I choose?
faq.answer: Use the admin variant by default. Choose per-user IDs for tenant-controlled apps or fallback mode when both options are required.

faq.question: Why must outcalls be non-replicated?
faq.answer: Replication sends authenticated requests multiple times, increases cycle and rate-limit costs, and expands bearer-token exposure.

faq.question: Is the provided OAuth flow complete?
faq.answer: No. Authorization, token exchange, and refresh functions are placeholders. Implement and review them before deployment.

faq.question: What protects the OAuth callback?
faq.answer: Use PKCE and a server-generated, one-time state value bound to the caller. Validate both before exchanging the authorization code.
